title: A boolean filter argument is the same as FILTER over ALL of the column
query: DEFINE MEASURE Sales[Red Sales] = CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], 'Product'[Color] = "Red" )
MEASURE Sales[Red Sales Full] = CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], FILTER ( ALL ( 'Product'[Color] ), 'Product'[Color] = "Red" ) )
EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS ( 'Product'[Color], "Red Sales", [Red Sales], "Red Sales Full", [Red Sales Full] )

source.quote: the predicate shown in the first expression is internally converted in the second expression
source.supports: a predicate on one column is converted to FILTER ( ALL ( column ), predicate )

source.quote: The result of this filter will override any existing filter over the specified columns.
source.supports: a filter built on ALL of a column overrides the existing filter on that column

derivation: ALL ( Product[Color] ) is Red, Blue, Green whatever the current color; FILTER keeps Red; the resulting filter on Color replaces the row's. Both measures give Red sales, 460, on each of the three color rows.
notes: SUM of a fixed decimal (currency) column is taken to be a fixed decimal, as in the seed cases.
